inspection.visible_text: The Tribe Network Skip to content The Tribe Network Skip to main content Free to join The Tribe Get practical support MEN • COMMUNITY • DIRECTION • PRACTICAL SUPPORT THE TRIBE NETWORK A community of men finding direction together. Belong. Speak freely. Share what you know. Learn from other men. Find your direction — and practical help when you need it. A place for adult men to connect through real conversation, useful knowledge, interests, practical experience and perspectives worth exploring. Free to join The Tribe Get practical support One community. Useful knowledge. Real interests. Practical help when discussion is not enough. BelongSpeak freelyShare what you knowLearn from other men WHY THE TRIBE NETWORK EXISTS Experience should travel. Every generation of men faces its own challenges. For much of human life, experience travelled between men — through fathers, brothers, friends, mentors and older men who had already walked part of the road. The Tribe Network exists to rebuild some of that connection in a modern, organised place. Why The Tribe exists A place to speak openly, think independently and become more capable in the lives we lead. Share experience. Learn from different perspectives. Explore useful ideas. Pass on practical knowledge. Ask for help when you need it. Not a hive mind. Not one man’s answer. A community of men finding direction together. THE TRIBE IN MOTION Ideas to return to. A changing glimpse of how the network thinks, learns and talks. PrincipleNo single book. No single philosophy. No final answer.Explore it. Question it. Compare it. Decide what is useful. Independent thoughtThink for yourself.Step outside the noise. Better questions create better judgement. Community cultureSpeak freely. Challenge honestly. Respect the tribe.Honest disagreement can make the room stronger. Community cultureChallenge the idea. Respect the man. Protect the room.Different views are welcome. Destructive behaviour is not the price of honesty. BoundaryMen’s issues do not require an enemy.A men’s community can be confident about men without being hostile to anybody else. PerspectiveCuriosity before ideology.Difficult subjects deserve intelligent conversation, not compulsory agreement. ExperienceExperience should travel.Men should be able to learn from men who have already walked part of the road. Personal growthStrength doesn’t mean emotionless.Sometimes strength is acting. Sometimes waiting. Sometimes asking for help. Intergenerational learningNot everybody knows everything. Everybody may know something worth passing on.Experience is perspective, not unquestionable authority. Founder philosophyBuilt from curiosity, not certainty.The aim is not to build another ideology. Community valueDiscover. Discuss. Contribute. Return.A useful community gives men reasons to come back. StandingCommunity standing is earned, not bought.Useful contribution and judgement matter more than status for sale. Resource integrityCommunity-shared does not mean automatically endorsed.Useful material can be explored without treating every source as doctrine. The Reading RoomBooks, articles and talks worth exploring.Good material gives men something to think about, even when they disagree with parts of it. Different VoicesChange the angle.Videos, interviews and podcasts can add context or challenge an assumption. The Men’s TableReal conversation about real life.Work, money, relationships, fatherhood, health, pressure, purpose and starting again. The WorkshopUseful knowledge is often learned by doing.DIY, repairs, practical skills, tools, projects and experience worth passing on. Off the ClockMen are more than their problems.Sport, cars, motorbikes, fishing, outdoors, gaming, technology and the things we simply enjoy. Field NotesLessons learned the hard way should not disappear.What worked, what did not and what somebody wishes they had understood earlier. PreviousPauseNext WHAT YOU’LL FIND INSIDE Conversation, interests and practical knowledge. The network should grow from genuine member demand. These are some of the places men may find common ground. Fatherhood & relationships Work & money Men’s health & wellbeing Books, ideas & culture Cars, DIY & practical skills Sport, fishing, outdoors & interests Pause spotlight Community standing is earned, not bought. The fuller set of rooms and interests belongs inside the network rather than turning Home into a catalogue. THE KNOWLEDGE SHELF Help The Tribe build the shelf. Books, YouTube videos, talks, articles, and ideas worth discussing. These are starting points. If something has helped you think and grow, bring it in. BOOKRobert Greene The 33 Strategies of War Not every conflict deserves a fight. Greene draws on military history to explore when to take the initiative, hold your position, negotiate or walk away, and how to keep a clear head while others react. Why The Tribe thinks it matters: A strong framework for thinking about conflict, timing, initiative, positioning, defence, negotiation and when not to fight.Founder’s takeawayUnderstand the terrain, control the pace, choose battles carefully, keep the initiative where useful, and avoid reactive or unwinnable moves. StrategySource ↗ BOOKRobert Greene The 48 Laws of Power Who holds the power, and how are they using it? Greene’s deliberately provocative laws examine influence, reputation and manipulation, offering a way to recognise the game without having to adopt every tactic. Why The Tribe thinks it matters: Useful as a map of power dynamics, status, reputation, incentives, influence and manipulation, especially for recognising what other people may be doing rather than copying every law.Founder’s takeawayPower often works indirectly. Before reacting, understand incentives, status, reputation, timing, leverage and possible manipulation. Human behaviourSource ↗ AUDIOBOOKNiccolò Machiavelli The Prince & The Art of War: The Definitive Collection on Statecraft and Military Tactics What keeps a ruler in power when ideals meet hard reality? These two works by Machiavelli examine political survival, leadership and military organisation, inviting you to question the distance between appearances and motives. Why The Tribe thinks it matters: A useful historical lens on power, statecraft, competition and human motives.Founder’s takeawayLook beneath appearances. Understand motives, incentives, power, reputation and the terrain before deciding how to act. StrategySource ↗ AUDIOBOOKAlan Watts Out of Your Mind: Essential Listening from the Alan Watts Audio Archives What happens when you question the identity and assumptions you take for granted? In these recorded talks, Watts draws on Eastern and Western traditions to challenge habitual thinking about the self and its place in the world. Why The Tribe thinks it matters: A perspective-shifting way to examine assumptions and look at familiar problems from another angle.Founder’s takeawaySometimes clarity comes from changing the frame: question the assumptions occupying your attention and look at the situation from another angle. PerspectiveSource ↗ AUDIOBOOKArnold Schwarzenegger Be Useful: Seven Tools for Life A clear vision is only the beginning. Schwarzenegger sets out seven practical tools for turning ambition into effort, learning from setbacks and making yourself useful to other people. Why The Tribe thinks it matters: Its emphasis on hard work, grit, reinvention, clear thinking and continuing to move when circumstances are difficult.Founder’s takeawayProgress usually requires useful action, sustained effort and resilience rather than waiting for ideal conditions. DisciplineSource ↗ AUDIOBOOKPaul Mcgee How Not to Worry: The Remarkable Truth of How a Small Change Can Help You Stress Less and Enjoy Life More When worry takes over, even a small problem can fill the room. McGee explores the thinking habits that keep it going and practical ways to regain perspective and move towards a constructive response. Why The Tribe thinks it matters: Worry, stress and anxiety can affect anyone, especially in a crisis.Founder’s takeawayWhen worry is consuming attention, useful tools can help separate the problem itself from the thinking that is amplifying it. StressSource ↗ AUDIOBOOKRobin Baker Sperm Wars: Infidelity, Sexual Conflict, and Other Bedroom Battles What might evolutionary competition explain about sex and attraction? Baker presents a provocative biological account through imagined scenarios and argument. It is a challenging perspective to examine, not a complete explanation of any individual. Why The Tribe thinks it matters: It offered a provocative evolutionary-biology lens on sexual and relationship behaviour and gave me another angle from which to reflect after relationship breakdown.Founder’s takeawayBiological and evolutionary explanations can be one lens on behaviour, but they should be tested against the individual facts rather than used as a complete explanation of a person. Human behaviourSource ↗ AUDIOBOOKThomas Erikson Surrounded by Idiots: The Four Types of Human Behaviour (or, How to Understand Those Who Cannot Be Understood) Why does a conversation work with one person and fall apart with another? Erikson uses a four-colour behaviour model to suggest ways of recognising communication differences and adjusting how you respond. Why The Tribe thinks it matters: A simple way to think about interpersonal differences, communication friction and why people can interpret the same situation very differently.Founder’s takeawayBefore reacting to someone’s style, consider whether the friction may come from different communication patterns, priorities or ways of processing. CommunicationSource ↗ AUDIOBOOKDavid M. Buss, Phd When Men Behave Badly: The Hidden Roots of Sexual Deception, Harassment, and Assault Why do deception, jealousy and sexual conflict arise in relationships? Buss explores them through an evolutionary lens, including the darker territory of harassment and coercion, to examine motives and potential warning signs. Why The Tribe thinks it matters: My collection should contain perspectives I agree with, partly agree with and challenge.Founder’s takeawayA strong resource bank should compare competing perspectives rather than treating agreement with one author as the goal. Human behaviourSource ↗ AUDIOBOOKMiyamoto Musashi The Complete Book of Five Rings A swordsman’s strategy reaches beyond the sword. Musashi’s writings explore perception, timing and disciplined practice, with historical context that helps you question what may still apply outside their original setting. Why The Tribe thinks it matters: The value goes beyond warfare: it explores discipline, control, timing, perception and life philosophy through an old strategic tradition.Founder’s takeawayAncient strategy can still be useful when translated into self-command, situational awareness and disciplined choices rather than literal conflict. StrategySource ↗ AUDIOBOOKRyan Holiday The Obstacle Is the Way: The Timeless Art of Turning Trials into Triumph The obstacle need not be the end of the road. Holiday draws on Stoic ideas and historical examples to explore how a different perspective, deliberate action and endurance can change your response to adversity. Why The Tribe thinks it matters: Stoicism offers a practical way to organise adversity: separate what is outside your control from the response that remains yours to choose.Founder’s takeawayYou may not control the situation or outcome, but you can work on the judgement, emotion and action you bring to it. ResilienceSource ↗ AUDIOBOOKFranco Augustus In Pursuit of Stoicism: The Inner Peace: How to Boost Your Mental Toughness and Achieve Emotional Resilience in This Modern Age You cannot organise every event around you. Augustus turns instead to the Stoic question of how to govern your own responses, introducing practices for emotional resilience and a steadier approach to everyday life. Why The Tribe thinks it matters: A practical companion to more historical or conceptual Stoic material because it focuses on applying the ideas in everyday life.Founder’s takeawayYou cannot control every event, but you can practise more deliberate control over attention, interpretation and response. Emotional controlSource ↗ AUDIOBOOKRobert Greene The Daily Laws: 366 Meditations on Power, Seduction, Mastery, Strategy, and Human Nature One short encounter with an idea, every day. Greene brings together lessons on power, strategy, self-understanding and mastery so that noticing human behaviour becomes a regular practice rather than a one-off insight. Why The Tribe thinks it matters: A daily source of short reflections on motivation, power, strategy, mastery, impulse, strengths, weaknesses and human nature.Founder’s takeawaySmall, repeated reflections can sharpen awareness of motives, behaviour and strategy without requiring every idea to be accepted. Human behaviourSource ↗ AUDIOBOOKGregory Lopez & Massimo Pigliucci Live Like a Stoic: 52 Exercises for Cultivating a Good Life How do you turn philosophy into something you actually practise? Lopez and Pigliucci offer a year of weekly Stoic exercises, with reflection and repetition that bring the ideas into ordinary situations. Why The Tribe thinks it matters: It turns Stoic ideas into exercises.Founder’s takeawayRead and listen widely, test the exercises, and keep the practices that genuinely help you become steadier and more resilient. ResilienceSource ↗ AUDIOBOOKRobert Greene The Laws of Human Nature What is driving the person in front of you, and what is driving you? Greene examines the motives beneath behaviour, inviting you to notice emotion, social masks and conformity before they make your decisions for you. Why The Tribe thinks it matters: It explores the drives and motivations that may operate beneath visible behaviour, including our own.Founder’s takeawayLook for motives and patterns, but use reflection to test your interpretation rather than assuming you can know what is inside another person’s mind. Human behaviourSource ↗ AUDIOBOOKDonald J. Robertson How to Think Like a Roman Emperor: The Stoic Philosophy of Marcus Aurelius How did a Roman emperor work at remaining steady under pressure? Robertson connects Marcus Aurelius’s life and Stoic philosophy with modern psychological practice, turning the historical story into exercises for everyday adversity. Why The Tribe thinks it matters: It combines Marcus Aurelius’s life with Stoic philosophy, giving historical context as well as a practical lens for adversity, composure and excellence.Founder’s takeawayHistory becomes useful when its principles help you meet present difficulty with clearer judgement and steadier action. ResilienceSource ↗ AUDIOBOOKSun Tzu The Art of War The most useful victory may be the battle you do not need to fight. Sun Tzu’s military classic invites close attention to preparation, conditions, timing and strategy before committing yourself to a costly confrontation. Why The Tribe thinks it matters: A cornerstone strategy text on preparation, positioning, timing, judgement and avoiding unnecessary disadvantage.Founder’s takeawayGood strategy begins with understanding the terrain, yourself and the other side, then choosing action carefully rather than reacting blindly. StrategySource ↗ AUDIOBOOKDerick Howell Eliminate Negative Thinking: How to Overcome Negativity, Control Your Thoughts, and Stop Overthinking. Shift Your Focus into Positive Thinking, Self-Acceptance, and Radical Self Love When thinking becomes an endless loop, more thinking is not always the answer. Howell offers self-help exercises aimed at recognising negative patterns, interrupting overthinking and developing a kinder relationship with yourself. Why The Tribe thinks it matters: A practical and reflective toolkit for negative thinking and overthinking.Founder’s takeawayUse self-help techniques experimentally: keep what improves your thinking and self-management rather than assuming one method fits everyone. Mental wellbeingSource ↗ AUDIOBOOKRollo Tomassi The Rational Male – Preventive Medicine What would you have approached differently had you understood it earlier? Tomassi’s follow-up presents his account of changing relationship dynamics across life stages. Read it as a perspective to examine, rather than a prediction about every woman. Why The Tribe thinks it matters: A follow-on perspective on male/female relationship dynamics and life-stage experiences, particularly for reflection after relationship difficulty.Founder’s takeawayRelationship theories can provide questions to explore, but they should never replace the actual facts, individuality and context of the people involved. Men and societySource ↗ AUDIOBOOKTom Hoobyar, Tom Dotz & Susan Sanders NLP: The Essential Guide to Neuro-Linguistic Programming Could noticing the way you think change the way you communicate? This practical NLP guide offers exercises in self-development and influence, inviting you to examine your habits rather than treating its promised results as guaranteed. Why The Tribe thinks it matters: Some NLP techniques can be useful for framing a situation, communicating more deliberately and thinking about how to move forward.Founder’s takeawayThe language and frame you use can affect how you organise a problem and the choices you notice, but framing should serve clarity rather than manipulation. CommunicationSource ↗ AUDIOBOOKRollo Tomassi The Rational Male Which beliefs about relationships have you examined for yourself? Tomassi collects his arguments about attraction and gender dynamics, challenging familiar assumptions through a deliberately contentious viewpoint that invites scrutiny as well as discussion. Why The Tribe thinks it matters: A prominent male-focused perspective on relationships and male/female dynamics, to compare with other viewpoints in the wider collection.Founder’s takeawayTake useful observations as prompts for reflection, but do not treat one relationship framework as a universal description of men, women or individual relationships. Men and societySource ↗ AUDIOBOOKRichard Cooper The Unplugged Alpha: The No BS Guide to Winning With Women & Life Are you building a life of your own or organising it around approval? Cooper challenges conventional dating advice and argues for putting personal development, purpose and boundaries first. His broader claims remain a viewpoint to test. Why The Tribe thinks it matters: It challenges conventional messages about male behaviour, relationships and social expectations and encourages independent examination rather than passive conformity.Founder’s takeawayQuestion inherited assumptions and social pressure, but test claims against evidence and your own circumstances instead of replacing one ‘herd’ view with another. MasculinitySource ↗ AUDIOBOOKAlan Roger Currie Mode One: Let the Women Know What You’re REALLY Thinking Are you saying what you mean, or hoping somebody will guess? Currie’s approach centres on direct, honest communication, especially with women you are interested in, and asks what changes when intentions are no longer hidden. Why The Tribe thinks it matters: Its discussion of modes of verbal communication still contained some useful ideas.Founder’s takeawayA resource does not need to be a favourite to be worth keeping; sometimes a few useful communication ideas are enough. CommunicationSource ↗ AUDIOBOOKDavid Deida The Way of the Superior Man: A Spiritual Guide to Mastering the Challenges of Women, Work, and Sexual Desire How do purpose, work, intimacy and desire fit into the same life? Deida approaches these questions through a spiritual view of masculinity, asking men to examine how they bring presence and direction to their relationships. Why The Tribe thinks it matters: Another perspective on male spirituality, purpose, work and relationships.Founder’s takeawayUse a range of perspectives to examine purpose, relationships and responsibility, then keep only what survives reflection and fits your circumstances. MasculinitySource ↗ OTHERJim Rohn The Day That Turns Your Life Around Change may begin with a decision rather than a dramatic event. Rohn explores how a moment of recognition can become deliberate action, asking what you are ready to do differently instead of waiting for circumstances to change. Why The Tribe thinks it matters: Practical self-development ideas that focus on translating useful thinking into deliberate action.Founder’s takeawayA useful idea only matters if it can be translated into deliberate action in ordinary life. MotivationSource ↗ OTHER ONLINE VIDEOGeorge Carlin George Carlin — Stand-Up & Social Commentary Familiar words and everyday conventions can look different when a comedian pulls them apart. Carlin’s stand-up invites you to notice language, contradictions and assumptions, and to decide for yourself where the challenge lands. Why The Tribe thinks it matters: A perspective-shifting voice rather than a conventional self-help source.Founder’s takeawayHumour can create useful distance from accepted assumptions and make it easier to question whether something makes sense simply because everyone repeats it. PerspectiveSource ↗ FOUNDER OBSERVATIONFounder Reflection No single book or philosophy has all the answers No single resource gets the last word. This founder reflection is an invitation to compare perspectives, keep what proves useful and continue developing your own judgement. Why The Tribe thinks it matters: This is the governing principle behind the collection: the value comes from comparing different viewpoints, not treating any author, philosophy or community as the complete answer.Founder’s takeawayRead and listen widely. Compare perspectives, reflect on your own experience, test ideas against evidence and context, and keep what genuinely proves useful. Critical thinkingFounder-captured resource PreviousPauseNext Curiosity, not endorsement. A resource appearing here does not mean The Tribe Network agrees with every view in it. FOUNDING MEMBERS Come in at the beginning. The first members will help shape the rooms, interests, conversations and culture of The Tribe Network. The aim is to grow from genuine member demand rather than pretend we already know what every future member will want. You can help shape something worth returning to. Free to join The Tribe WHEN IDEAS AREN’T ENOUGH Sometimes life stops being theoretical. A letter arrives. A relationship breaks down. Something changes at work. Money becomes tight. A deadline appears. Several problems hit at once. The Tribe Network gives you community, knowledge, interests and shared experience. Sometimes discussion is not enough. Start with what happened, work out where you stand and choose the next clear move. Free to understand. Paid to prepare. Understanding the problem and the likely route forward should provide genuine value. Paid preparation comes later only if you choose deeper help. Start by telling the story. We’ll help map the way forward. Get practical support now THE TRIBE NETWORK Find your direction. Find your people. Help build something worth returning to. Join the community or get practical support when life needs more than words.
